objective: ROOT-R01 proof-only transaction: characterize general P3 cut interfaces, prove exact gluing/counting and signature-inclusion reductions, with explicit small replacement tilings. Executable-code upload is blocked by a platform safety gate and is not part of this packet.

atomic_claims.text: Incidence-based U/A/B local realizations glue exactly by U-U and A-B compatibility; the global P3-factor count is the sum of products of compatible local counts, including repeated boundary vertices.
For r=2 and r=3 ports the arithmetic state tables are exactly the words with number(A)+2*number(B) congruent to the fragment order modulo three; feasibility remains a separate condition.

A three-port triangle realizes eight of nine residue-zero words, missing BBB; a singleton with three ports realizes only the six leaf/center words. These are auxiliary signature counterexamples, not root counterexamples.

A smaller same-residue fragment with a signature subset of the original can replace it whenever simplicity, cubicity and 3-connectivity are preserved; this excludes the original fragment from a smallest root counterexample.
The C04 complete Petersen-minus-vertex signature includes the triangle signature, so that nine-vertex brick cannot be a three-cut side in a smallest root counterexample.
The explicitly listed five-vertex triangular-prism fragment realizes all nine residue-two words, with nine hand-checkable tilings.

assumptions: Finite simple graphs; cubic means degree three; 3-connected means vertex connectivity at least three.
P3 is a selected two-edge path, not necessarily induced.
Fragment ports are indexed incidences; repeated vertices require the two-outgoing-port center tile.
Allowed axioms remain finite-graph-basic and finite-combinatorics.
